title: personal-results-commitment-contract
content:
Personal Results Commitment Contract — working draft
Owner: Ryan Glover (eng-serving-runtime)
Quarter: Q1 2026 (personal focus window: Jan 18 -> Apr 3)
Purpose: Create a compact commitment doc I can share with manager at the 1:1 that sets clear measureable outcomes, explicit acceptance criteria, and a weekly check-in cadence. Treat this like a lightweight contract: what I will ship, how we will measure it, and what to do if things slip.

---
Top-level objective (draft)
Objective: Reduce 95th percentile tail latency for small-text generation requests (<=128 tokens) across staged models on staging fleet while holding cost per token within current budget band.
Why this matters: Improves UX for interactive features and reduces fallback risk for hosted customers. Also reduces SLA risk on Dedicated fleets.

Proposed Key Results (KR) — measurable and timebound
KR1: 95th percentile latency drops from baseline 420ms to <=310ms across a representative 10k request sample on staging by Mar 15. (Metric: p95 latency, 10k sample same distribution as production)
KR2: End-to-end average cost per token (inference compute cost + infra overhead) does not increase >2% relative to Jan baseline when optimizations are live. (Metric: normalized cost/tk)
KR3: Ship two targeted optimizations in serving runtime: (a) split-prefix KV cache for short chats, (b) dynamic small-batch path with JIT kernel selection; both with unit tests and perf harness.

Acceptance criteria (what counts as done)
- Perf harness validated: synthetic + production-like trace run with runbook documenting load shape and results.
- Rollout plan: canary on 5% staging traffic, automated rollback if error rate increases >0.5% or latency regression >10% on p95.
- PRs merged, perf dashboard updated with baseline and comparison panels, one-pager for SRE and product.

Weekly checkpoints (what I will bring to 1:1)
- Week 0 (Jan 18): Baseline numbers, experiment plan, test harness checklist.
- Week 1: KV cache prototype + microbench results; list of unknowns.
- Week 2: Small-batch dynamic path initial implementation + unit perf numbers.
- Week 3: Integration harness run, first end-to-end numbers.
- Week 4: Canary rollout on staging, monitor metrics, remediation notes.

Risks & mitigations (short form)
- Risk: Optimizations change output ordering or determinism for a small fraction of queries.
  Mitigation: Add automated diff harness on sampled requests and threshold for acceptable diffs tied to quality team review.
- Risk: Cost increases due to additional kernel overhead.
  Mitigation: Track cost/tk tradeoffs, gate rollout behind cost budget test.

Hypotheses to test (experiments)
- Hypothesis A: Prefix-split KV cache reduces repeated attention compute by ~25% for short sessions resulting in ~18% p95 reduction. Experiment: A/B with 50/50 traffic split using synthetic short chat traces.
- Hypothesis B: Dynamic small-batch path yields higher utilization on spare GPUs without impacting median latency. Experiment: compare utilization and p50/p95 under same load shape with and without path enabled.

Implementation notes & checklist
- [ ] Create perf harness story and link JIRA (JIRA-RT-312).
- [ ] Prototype KV split in serving-runtime branch (branch: rgl/kvsplit-short).
- [ ] Add unit and integration perf tests (target CI extra-runs).
- [ ] Instrument new metrics: kv_hit_ratio_short, dynamic_batch_enabled, p95_short_requests.
- [ ] Draft canary runbook and rollback steps — share with SRE and product.

Personal guardrails (non-technical)
- Timebox: 10 focused hours per week on core work; remaining time for code reviews and mentoring. If spike >2 weeks, escalate to manager and propose re-prioritization.
- Communication: Weekly short email to stakeholders summarizing progress + one open question for feedback.

Open questions for manager 1:1
- Is the cost guardrail (<=2% increase) acceptable or should I tighten to 0%?
- Are there any customers or routes we should exclude from canary to reduce noisier workloads?
- Priority tradeoffs: if early evidence suggests cost savings but increased tail for a specific model, do we prefer roll-forward or rollback?

Notes to self (scratchpad bits)
- Remember to re-run production-like traces during off-peak to avoid collateral noise in telemetry.
- Talk to Maya about dashboard layout: want side-by-side p50/p95/cost panels.
- Quick perf wins to try if stalled: smaller fp quantization experiments on staging-only models; input length bucketing for batching heuristics.

Archive / iteration plan
- Save snapshot of this doc before major changes (filename: personal-results-commitment-contract-ryan-glover-v1).
- After Mar 15: convert to retrospective note: what worked, what didn't, metric delta.

Bottom line (commitment sentence)
I commit to deliver the above KRs or surface substantive blockers by weekly check-ins; if progress stalls I will propose a concrete mitigation plan and timeline.

---
End of working draft — notes are intentionally terse; will expand before sharing in 1:1.
